records.escapeReason: the closed-set invariant was documented in a comment but enforced on only one of three authored surfaces -- conditions and ops accepted any string, deferring a define-time fault to a non-SkillResolverError mid-execute crash that bypassed the decline lane entirely
applicability: any closed-domain id authored across multiple validator surfaces (resource, buff, definition, intent)
test fixtures must author in-set ids or they encode the bug as expected behavior
proposedProtection: one shared closed set constant guards every authored surface for the domain (RESOURCE_IDS on queries + conditions + ops)
pin tests assert the fault on EACH surface, not just the first found
comments stating an invariant get an enforcing check or get corrected

records.escapeReason: a decline lane that can fire after the commit point converts a real failure into a lie: cooldown spent + cost consumed + partial ops applied, stamped as a clean no-op -- any deferred resolution inside a committing plan must resolve before the commit or escalate as a fault, never masquerade
applicability: any commit-then-defer execution plan (composite extras, deferred charge-resolve, follow-up lanes)
error-to-null conversion boundaries must sit BEFORE the commit port
proposedProtection: resolve every deferred member pre-commit inside the plan; keep execution order unchanged
decline lanes get explicit 3-way classification (whiff/dangling/decline) so silent misclassification cannot recur

records.escapeReason: two independent gates encoded the wrong identity: once counted unpaid attempts as consumed rolls, and the income gate compared only the resolved payload id when the semantics were "the actor's basic" -- identity/counting gates need their exact semantic stated, not the nearest available value
applicability: identity gates (payload vs root vs variant ids)
proposedProtection: "once" counts the consumed resource (paid roll), not the attempt
identity gates compare every id that can name the entity (payload pick, variant, root def)
